text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- On Saturday Latvians remembered the victims of June 14, 1941, when tens of thousands of people were deported to Siberia by the Soviet regime.

- International auditor Deloitte & Touche announced the results of the competition to choose candidates for the post of technical director and that of the director of the privatisation process in the Latvian Privatisation Agency. The current directors retained their posts.
- 28 MPs representing the ruling coalition parties introduced a bill suggesting that MPs salaries be 75 percent of ministers. As a result, monthly earnings would grow from 314 to 461 lats.
- Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs admitted that a scandal over ministers combining official and private posts may throw Latvia several years back on its path to the EU.
- Parliament speaker Alfreds Chepanis is reported to have denied accomodation in the parliament hotel to a Chechen parliamentary delegation due on Monday.
- The Daugavpils-based textile works Dauteks was sold on Saturday for one lat to Asean Interests Limited, a member of Singapore's Tolaram Group.
- Visiting the U.S., Birkavs expressed the hope that the expansion of NATO would be as regular as the Olympic games not just once a lifetime like the Hale-Bopp comet.
- The event of the last week: shares of pharmaceutical company Olainfarm started on the Riga stock exchange.
- The former state minister for forestry, Arvids Ozols, was appointed deputy state secretary of the agriculture ministry in charge of the forestry sector.
